name: Frost slash flurry: 2D cut-in panel, then a wide shot of crescent slashes over a frost-splatter floor with a dark shard dome

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:00.0-0:02.4. Wide, low shot of the swordsman in a dark blue night arena, one thin white blade glint along the sword; nothing else on screen

phases.name: release
phases.what: hard cut to a flat full-screen cut-in panel: saturated cyan/teal field with one huge diagonal white-cream blade stroke (0:00.25), then the panel shatters into jagged white and blue 2D shards that fly past camera (0:00.4-0:00.6)

phases.name: impact
phases.what: cut back to the 3D wide shot: 6-8 fast thin white slash lines and crescent arcs criss-cross the character, the floor is covered in a white frost-splatter decal with radial streaks, a half-dome of dark broken shards snaps up behind the character on two beats (0:01.1 and 0:01.75), and on each beat the character flashes to a flat saturated-blue silhouette

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: flakes keep drifting, the splatter fades, the whole frame fades to black over 0.4 s (scene transition into the next cutscene)

layers.motion: full-screen flat colour panel for 2 frames with one diagonal cream blade shape, then broken into 10-15 shards that scale up and fly toward camera over 0.25 s
layers.notes: a 2D cut-in card instead of a 3D flash: flat colours, no gradients, hard polygon edges

layers.motion: 6-8 thin slash lines and crescent arcs at random angles around the target, each drawn in 2 frames and erased in 3, staggered ~0.12 s
layers.notes: very thin and long (3-5 m) so they read as cuts, never as glows

layers.motion: frost-splatter disc ~8 m with radial brush streaks, appears at full size in 1 frame, opacity flickers on each slash beat, fades over 0.6 s
layers.notes: the floor lights up white so the dark character pops against it; radial streaks point at the target

layers.motion: half-dome of 12-16 tall dark shard slabs arranged on a 5 m arc behind the target, pop up in 2 frames on each beat and sink back in 0.2 s
layers.notes: dark shapes frame the bright floor and character from behind like a stage set

layers.motion: target turns into a flat saturated-blue silhouette with a white rim for 2 frames on each big beat
layers.notes: colour-swap of the target instead of a white flash: the hit reads without blowing out the frame

layers.motion: flat white ice flakes, random rotation, slow fall with gravity 1, drag 2, life 1.2 s
layers.notes: flakes, not streaks: snow-like flecks keep the air busy between slashes

layers.motion: small sharp shakes on each slash beat, one bigger shake on the two dome beats
fade to black over 0.4 s
layers.notes: clean exit that doubles as the cut into the finisher cutscene

whyItLooksGood: The 0.35 s flat cyan cut-in panel tells the viewer 'special move' before any 3D effect plays: it works like a manga panel inserted between gameplay frames
The floor, not the air, is the brightest surface: a white frost splatter under a dark character gives a strong silhouette without any glow
The dark shard dome behind the target frames the action and only appears on the two heavy beats, so the flurry has a rhythm (many light cuts, two heavy)
The target flashing flat saturated blue instead of white keeps the whole effect inside one hue family
buildNotes: Video 0:00.0-0:02.4. Camera: start on a low wide shot; at 0.25 s overlay a full-screen orthographic quad (flat cyan with one cream diagonal blade polygon) for 0.15 s, then split that card into ~12 triangle shards that scale 1 -> 1.6 and fly outward over 0.2 s (a screen-space shard pass, or a camera-attached plane of instanced triangles). Back in world: slash lines are thin quads with an alpha-erosion shader (erode from tail to tip over 3 frames), spawn 6-8 at random yaw/roll around the target 0.12 s apart. Floor: one ground-decal sprite with a radial streak texture, additive white/blue, flicker opacity on each beat. Dome: instanced debris of 14 tall thin dark boxes on a 160 degree arc behind the target (relative to camera), tween scale-y 0 -> 1 in 2 frames on beats at 0.5 s and 1.15 s, then sink. Target colour swap: swap the dummy material to flat #1f2fff for 2 frames. Emitter: flat flakes with spin, gravity 1, drag 2. Fade to black via FinishPass at the end. Exaggerate the cut-in: make the blade stroke cover half the screen.

name: Frozen orb finisher cutscene: black-void orb close-up, ink impact frames, giant crystal shatter and whiteout

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:02.4-0:08.9 (white hold until ~0:11.5 trimmed). 0.4 s of pure black, then a cut to a pure-black void: a white-blue orb at screen centre inside 4-5 concentric thin rings, a red ribbon and a rainbow arc sweep around it, a horizontal lens streak and 2-3 white capsule bars slide in; the camera holds and slowly pushes in for 1.6 s while flecks drift

phases.name: release
phases.what: cut to a close-up of the character drawing the sword (0.25 s), then 2-3 frames of pure black-and-white ink impact frames (jagged black shapes on white), then one thin white slash line across a black screen with crystal shards bursting from it

phases.name: impact
phases.what: low-angle shot of the target encased in dark blue crystal slabs with a white sun-burst behind; at 3.5 s a giant ice crystal spire, white vertical capsule bars flying in from both sides, red streaks and a central white star; at 4.25 s a second set of B/W ink frames (black brush streaks on white, a thin crosshair line), then the crystal shatters into shards with a growing white glare

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: the glare fills the screen: full white with a soft grey vignette, held, then (in the video) a fade to black

layers.motion: orb fixed at screen centre, slow pulse 0.9-1.0 scale, 4-5 thin concentric rings rotating at different speeds
layers.notes: set on a pure black background so the orb is the only value in frame

layers.motion: one red smoke-like ribbon and one rainbow arc sweep in a wide circle around the orb over 0.6 s, then fade
layers.notes: the only non-blue colours in the shot; a complementary accent sweeping past

layers.motion: horizontal anamorphic lens streak through the orb plus 2-3 rounded white capsule bars that slide in from the edges and stop
layers.notes: graphic UI-like bars make the shot feel designed, like a title card

layers.motion: 2-3 frames of pure black/white ink frames: jagged black polygons on white, then inverted
layers.notes: zero colour for 3 frames resets the eye before the blue crystal shot

layers.motion: tall angular crystal slabs around the target, then shatter outward toward camera with spin, drag 1.5
layers.notes: dark saturated blue crystals with white edge highlights; hard faceted shapes

layers.motion: 6 white rounded capsule bars fly in vertically from both sides of the frame and lock in place around the target for 0.7 s
layers.notes: reads like a cage closing; strong vertical rhythm

layers.motion: white four-point star at the target with thin red streaks crossing it, then grows into full glare
white fills the screen with a soft grey vignette, held ~1 s, then fade to black
layers.notes: whiteout as the exit: the kill happens off-screen inside the white

layers.motion: heavy shake on the first frame after each ink-frame pair

whyItLooksGood: The orb shot happens in a black void, not in the arena: removing the environment for 1.6 s makes the next return to 3D feel like a hit
The camera holds still on the orb far longer than gameplay would allow; the stillness is the anticipation
Two ink-frame pairs split the finisher into 'cut' and 'shatter' beats, so a 6 s sequence reads as two clear hits
White capsule bars are a non-diegetic graphic that cages the target; they make the shot look composed rather than simulated
Ending on a held white screen means the effect never has to show its own clean-up
buildNotes: Video 0:02.4-0:08.9 (then white hold). This needs a scripted camera and a 'void' set. 0-0.4 s: FinishPass fade to black. 0.4-2.0 s: hide the arena (or render a camera-facing black backdrop plane behind a separate group) and place the orb GlowSphere 3 m in front of the camera; 5 createRing rings at different radii, each spinning on z at its own speed; one red trail-ribbon and one rainbow-gradient ribbon on a circular path; a horizontal stretched additive quad as lens streak; 3 rounded-rect white quads sliding in with ease-out. Push the camera in 15% over 1.6 s. 2.0 s: cut to a close-up of the caster (camera 1.5 m from the chest, low angle). 2.25 s: three FinishPass frames: black/white posterised ink frame (threshold the scene to 2 values plus a jagged black polygon overlay), then the inverse. 2.5 s: black screen with a single thin white slash quad across it and a shard burst from its centre. 2.75 s: restore the arena, camera low behind the target looking up; spawn instanced crystal slabs (dark blue MeshStandard with white rim) around the target. 3.5 s: tall crystal spire mesh, 6 white capsule quads fly in from screen edges and lock. 4.25 s: second ink-frame pair with brush-streak overlay and a thin crosshair line. 4.6 s: shatter the crystals (debris emitter with spin and drag) and ramp FinishPass white to 100% by 5.5 s, hold, fade to black. Exaggerate the void: no ground, no sky, nothing but the orb.

name: Fuga-style fire arrow: swirling flame charge, fire bow ring, black-ribbon release and a towering fire pillar at the target

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:07.0-0:12.0 (same effect also at 0:00.7, 0:15.3 and 0:20.0). A flat, horizontal disc of swirling flame whips around the caster at waist height with white wind streaks trailing it; short vertical flame spikes flick up from it every ~0.3 s, black scrap-like curls and embers spit outward, a dark smoke wisp rises

phases.name: release
phases.what: a bright thin golden circle (the 'bow') snaps open in front of the caster facing the target (2.25-2.6), then the arrow fires: a fan-shaped fire blast with large black-red ribbon curls bursting toward the target (2.6-2.85)

phases.name: impact
phases.what: at the target (6-10 m away) a tall, narrow white-yellow fire pillar erupts to ~4x character height; around its base big flame petals and black-red ribbon curls whip outward and up; the pillar flickers in width every few frames

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: the pillar collapses into a few licking flame tongues and is gone in ~0.3 s, leaving a faint dark scorch on the ground

layers.motion: flat disc of 3-4 flame ribbons orbiting the caster at 1 m radius, 2 rev/s, slightly tilted toward camera
layers.notes: a flat horizontal swirl, not a sphere: reads as winding up

layers.motion: white wind streaks trailing the flame disc, stretched along velocity, life 0.25 s
layers.notes: white air streaks give the spin speed

layers.motion: black curled scraps spat outward from the disc, spin 6, drag 2, gravity 3, life 0.5 s
layers.notes: dark curls like burnt paper make the fire look dangerous, not cosy

layers.motion: thin golden circle 1.5 m, vertical, facing the target, snaps open in 1 frame, holds 0.3 s, then the arrow punches through it
layers.notes: the bow ring is the readable cue that a shot is coming and from where

layers.motion: 4-6 large black-red ribbon curls fan outward toward the target in 0.2 s, then curl and fade
layers.notes: normal-blended dark ribbons with a hot edge; they carry the direction of the shot

layers.motion: narrow pillar 0.8 m wide x 10 m tall, rises in 2 frames, width flickers 0.8-1.2 every 3 frames, holds 1.5 s
layers.notes: white core with yellow-orange edges; its height is the payoff

layers.motion: large flame-petal sprites around the pillar base whipping outward and upward, spin, life 0.4 s
layers.notes: hand-drawn-looking flame tongues, not smoke

layers.motion: black-red ribbon curls thrown out from the base, gravity 4
layers.notes: repeat of the release darks so caster and target share a look

layers.motion: dark scorch ~3 m under the pillar, fades over 1 s
medium shake when the pillar rises

whyItLooksGood: The motion turns 90 degrees: a flat horizontal swirl and a horizontal shot become a vertical pillar at the target, so the impact reads as a new event and not just 'the projectile arrived'
The thin golden bow ring is a single clean shape inside a busy fire swirl; it is the only perfect circle in the effect, so the eye locks on it right before the shot
Black-red ribbon curls appear both at the release and at the pillar base, linking caster and target
The charge is long (2.25 s) and noisy, the shot is 0.25 s and clean: a strong timing contrast
buildNotes: Video 0:07.0-0:12.0. Charge: 3-4 flame trail-ribbons (scrolling-UV flame texture) on circular paths at 1 m radius around the caster, waist height, 2 rev/s; add an Emitter of stretched white wind streaks (velocity-aligned) and an Emitter of dark curl sprites (normal blend, spin 6, drag 2, gravity 3). Every 0.3 s spawn a short vertical flame spike billboard. Bow: createRing, vertical, oriented toward the target, thin and golden, snap scale 0 -> 1 in 1 frame. Release: 5 dark ribbon meshes (alpha-erosion shader, hot orange edge) that sweep out in a fan toward the target over 0.2 s; a fast small fireball streak (mesh-projectile, 0.15 s flight). Impact: LightPillar 0.8 x 10 m with flickering width; Emitter of large flame petal sprites at the base (spin, up-velocity 6, drag 1.5); dark curl emitter again; GlowSphere at the base. Camera shake medium on pillar birth. Exaggerate the pillar height and keep it narrow.

name: Dragon summon cutscene: spear crackle close-up, twin sky beams, dragon silhouette rising between them, whip-pan into a claw close-up

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:00.3-0:04.6. Slow close-up pan across the caster's flowered armour (0.25 s), then the spear crackles with white-violet lightning (0.25 s), cut to a wide shot of the caster on a violet flower field raising the spear (0.15 s)

phases.name: release
phases.what: low ground-level shot: a cluster of pink crystal spikes bursts from the ground, then two parallel violet-white beams slam down diagonally from the sky into the field, flowers and pink motes blasting up

phases.name: impact
phases.what: between the beams a huge dark dragon silhouette rises: two spiked arms/wings lined with glowing pink quills frame a black void, a single red glowing eye slit appears at its centre, butterflies and petals swirl; held 0.9 s with a slow push-in

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: a 1-frame dark close-up, then a 0.4 s diagonal violet speed-smear whip-pan, landing on a slow low-angle drift along the dragon's spiked neck with pink flame-like quills and a dripping moon in the starry sky, petals falling (1.3 s), then a short close-up of the caster's face to close

layers.motion: short jagged arcs crawling along the spear, redrawn every 2 frames
layers.notes: small and close: the power is shown on the weapon before anything big happens

layers.motion: cluster of 8-12 crystal spikes bursting up from one point, scale 0 -> 1 in 3 frames
layers.notes: pink faceted spikes; first beat of the summon

layers.motion: two parallel slanted beams (20 degrees off vertical) slam from sky to ground in 2 frames, hold 0.8 s with scrolling streaks inside
layers.notes: parallel twin beams act as the doorway the dragon rises through

layers.motion: giant dark silhouette (two spiked arms forming a U) rises from below frame over 0.6 s; pink quill spikes along its edges flicker
layers.notes: the dragon is mostly black; only its quills and eye are bright

layers.motion: thin horizontal red eye slit opens at the centre of the black shape, with a short horizontal lens streak
layers.notes: the smallest element in the shot is the focal point

layers.motion: butterfly and petal sprites fluttering upward, sine wobble, life 1.5 s
layers.notes: a themed particle (butterflies) instead of generic sparks

layers.motion: full-screen diagonal speed-smear (motion blur streaks) for 0.4 s as the camera whip-pans
layers.notes: the transition itself is a VFX layer

layers.motion: petals falling slowly across the claw close-up, gravity 0.5

whyItLooksGood: Shot sizes alternate on purpose: close-up (detail) -> wide (context) -> ground-level (scale) -> silhouette (reveal); each cut is under 0.3 s until the reveal, which is held
The twin beams create a frame-within-the-frame; the dragon appears inside that doorway so its arrival is staged, not spawned
The dragon is a black shape with a red slit eye: maximum mystery, cheap to build, and the single red accent in a violet scene is impossible to miss
The whip-pan smear hides the cut between two very different angles and keeps momentum
buildNotes: Video 0:00.3-0:04.6. Camera script: (1) 0-0.25 s close-up 1.5 m from caster chest, slow lateral dolly; (2) 0.25-0.5 s close on spear with lightning-arc ribbons; (3) 0.5-0.65 s wide shot; (4) 0.65-1.5 s camera at 0.3 m height looking up past the summon point; (5) 1.5-2.4 s same angle, slow push-in 10%; (6) 2.4-2.8 s whip-pan (rotate camera 60 degrees in 0.3 s plus a full-screen diagonal streak overlay); (7) 2.8-4.1 s low-angle drift along the dragon body toward a moon sprite; (8) 4.1-4.3 s caster face close-up. Darken the world to violet for the whole sequence. Crystal spikes: instanced debris of stretched octahedra, additive pink. Beams: two LightPillar meshes tilted 20 degrees. Dragon: a custom black silhouette mesh (two spiked arcs) with an additive pink quill strip along the edges; a tiny red additive quad as the eye. Butterflies: Emitter with a butterfly sprite, sine wobble, upward drift. Exaggerate the size of the silhouette (fills 70% of the frame) and keep it unlit black.

name: Wing nova finisher: butterfly whip-pans, spiked wings opening with orbiting ribbons, ring-core charge, ink frame and a giant pink sphere blast on the field

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:05.1-0:09.6. Wide shot: the caster with a white flower-petal shock burst along the ground and the dragon behind (0.6 s); 0.6 s diagonal violet smear with butterflies flying through (whip-pan); 1 frame flat cream flash; 1 frame of big flat pink/yellow graphic shapes; a short ground-level shot with a lightning crack

phases.name: release
phases.what: front-on shot of the dragon in a starry void with a dripping moon: spiked dark wings spread, magenta curved ribbons orbit it, red ribbons cross behind; at 2.6 s a white hollow ring with a bright core forms at its chest, then a red spike starburst and a white ray starburst (1 frame each)

phases.name: impact
phases.what: a dithered white flash frame, then one ink impact frame (white screen, black silhouettes of the field edge), then the result shot

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: back on the flower field: a huge glowing pink-white sphere sits on the ground filling half the screen, a dark butterfly/eye silhouette inside it, violet flames licking its base, dark rock chunks flying out and slowly falling; held ~1.2 s

layers.motion: white flower-petal shards burst along the ground in a fan, drag 2
full-screen diagonal smear with butterfly sprites flying through it, 0.6 s
layers.notes: whip-pan used as a breather between shots

layers.motion: spiked dark wing shapes unfold from the centre outward over 0.4 s
layers.notes: dark wings with white-lilac edge highlights

layers.motion: 8-10 thin curved ribbons orbit the dragon on tilted circular paths, fast, with long tails
layers.notes: thin magenta loops make a 'charging' cage around the dark shape

layers.motion: white hollow ring 3 m around a bright core at the chest, appears in 1 frame, then pinches in
layers.notes: implode cue before the blast

layers.motion: red spike starburst for 1 frame, then a white ray starburst for 1 frame
layers.notes: two starbursts in two colours read as a double strike

layers.motion: 1 frame dithered white (visible dot pattern), 1 frame pure white with black silhouettes
layers.notes: a dither pattern on the flash frame gives a retro print texture

layers.motion: giant sphere half-buried in the ground, 10 m, appears at full size and slowly breathes; a dark silhouette symbol floats inside
layers.notes: the result is a big static shape held for a beat, like a key art frame

layers.motion: dark rock chunks flung outward and up, slow fall, spin
layers.notes: dark debris in front of the bright sphere gives depth

layers.motion: heavy shake for 0.3 s on the first result frame, then still

whyItLooksGood: The charge shot is staged in a separate starry void with the moon, so it reads as a 'special move' space; the result cuts back to the real field to show consequence
Orbiting thin magenta ribbons around a dark wing shape keep the charge alive without adding brightness
The result is shown as one huge held shape (a sphere with a symbol inside) rather than a chaotic explosion: it reads in a single glance
Flat 1-frame graphic cards (cream flash, pink/yellow shapes) between shots add punch without costing screen time
buildNotes: Video 0:05.1-0:09.6. Camera script: (1) wide shot of caster, 0.6 s; (2) whip-pan smear 0.6 s (rotate camera fast plus diagonal streak overlay with butterfly sprites); (3) two single-frame FinishPass cards (flat cream, then big flat pink/yellow polygons); (4) 0.2 s ground-level shot; (5) front-on shot of the summon on a void backdrop (black plane with star sprites and a moon sprite with a drip texture), slow push-in; (6) flash frames; (7) cut to a wide low shot of the arena for the sphere. Build: wings as a custom spiked mesh unfolding by scale/rotation tween; 8-10 trail-ribbons on tilted circular paths; createRing white hollow ring that scales 1 -> 0.2 over 0.25 s (implode); two 1-frame starburst sprites (red, white); FinishPass: dithered white frame (ordered-dither shader on the flash) then pure white with the scene thresholded to black silhouettes. Result: a 10 m GlowSphere half under the ground at the target cluster centre, a dark butterfly sprite inside, instanced dark debris with gravity 4 and spin. Exaggerate the sphere size and hold it still.

name: Dragon breath over-the-shoulder cutscene: thin beam into a crater, three escalating impact stages split by inverted frames

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:00.0-0:14.7, compressed (each impact stage loops for several seconds in the video). Over-the-shoulder shot from behind the dragon's head: a pale pink-white flame mane on the left of frame, a thin glowing magenta scythe line across it, a magenta glow building in the mouth; the target crater sits small in the upper right

phases.name: release
phases.what: a thin straight beam (white core, cyan and magenta edges) shoots from the mouth into the crater

phases.name: impact
phases.what: stage 1 (video 0:02.4-0:04.4): blue-white splash at the crater with dark violet smoke boiling up around its rim, the camera re-frames with a small shake

phases.name: impact
phases.what: stage 2 (video 0:04.4-0:06.6): the hit turns into a magenta-white spiky starburst with radial cracks in the ground

phases.name: impact
phases.what: 1 frame inverted/posterised frame (black with white and acid-green shapes, video 0:06.7), then stage 3: an orange-gold fire explosion with spiky rays and square ground slabs lifting and tilting out of the crater; a second inverted frame at video 0:09.0 restarts the explosion; it sustains with flicker

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: hard cut to a calm wide gameplay shot of the field (no fade)

layers.motion: mouth glow grows 0.2 -> 0.8 m with flicker
thin beam 0.2 m, scrolling UV, appears from mouth to target in 2 frames, width wobbles
layers.notes: thin and long: the scale contrast with the huge impact sells the power

layers.motion: dark violet smoke boiling up around the crater rim, drag 2, slow rise
layers.notes: dark ring framing the bright splash

layers.motion: stage 1 blue-white splash; stage 2 magenta spiky starburst re-randomised every 3 frames
layers.notes: the same hit changes colour as it escalates

layers.motion: radial crack lines spreading out from the hit point over 0.5 s
1 frame posterised inversion: black background, white highlights, acid-green mid-tones
layers.notes: an inverted frame with an off-palette green is the stage switch

layers.motion: stage 3: radial spiky ray sprites and sparks, short life 0.15 s, re-spawned continuously
layers.notes: gold fire against a violet world: complementary colour on the final stage

layers.motion: 8-12 square ground slabs lift 0.5-1.5 m and tilt out of the crater, hover, glowing orange edges underneath
layers.notes: big flat slabs, not small rocks: the ground itself breaks

layers.motion: constant small shake during the stages, heavy shake after each inverted frame

whyItLooksGood: Over-the-shoulder framing with the dragon's huge pale mane filling a third of the frame makes the target small and the attacker enormous
The impact escalates in three colour stages (blue -> magenta -> gold), each switch marked by a single inverted frame, so a long channel keeps getting bigger instead of just lasting
A thin beam into a huge explosion: the cause is tiny, the result is massive
Lifting square ground slabs read as the floor breaking, which feels heavier than any particle
buildNotes: Video 0:00.0-0:14.7 (compress each stage to ~1 s in game). Camera: place the camera behind and slightly above the caster's head, offset to one side, looking at the target; put a large pale foreground shape (custom flame-mane mesh or a big billboard) at the left edge to create the over-the-shoulder frame. Beam: beam-ribbon with scrolling-UV shader, white core with cyan/magenta edges. Stage 1: GlowSphere blue-white at the target plus normal-blended dark violet smoke Emitter on a ring (drag 2). Stage 2: swap to a magenta starburst sprite (re-randomise rotation every 3 frames) and an additive crack decal. Stage switch: one FinishPass frame that inverts and posterises (black / white / #7aff3a). Stage 3: gold ray-burst sprites, spark Emitter, instanced square slabs that tween up and tilt with an emissive orange bottom face; second invert frame halfway. End on a hard cut to the gameplay camera. Exaggerate the size jump of each stage.

name: Void moon wedge sweep: pink hand sigil, horizontal flare, then a giant black wedge with a dark moon slashing across the field inside a magenta swirl

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:15.9-0:17.7. A small pink ring sigil with a bright core appears at the caster's raised hand (0.15-0.35), then collapses into a flat horizontal pink flare line (0.35-0.45)

phases.name: release
phases.what: a giant magenta crescent swirl wraps around the caster and a huge black wedge shape slashes diagonally across the whole field toward the target

phases.name: impact
phases.what: the wedge holds: a dark moon sphere with a shadow figure inside sits in the black band, several pink-white streaks run along the wedge edges, butterflies and petal confetti scatter, the swirl fades

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: the wedge thins into a few streaks and vanishes; a low violet dust cloud and floating pink motes remain around the caster and target

layers.motion: 0.6 m ring with bright core at the hand, appears in 1 frame, then squashes vertically into a line
layers.notes: tiny and precise: the whole move is cued by one small shape

layers.motion: horizontal flare streak 3 m wide, 2 frames
thick crescent swirl, 1.5 turns around the caster, 0.15 s, then erodes
huge black wedge (25 m long, 4 m tall at its thick end) slides diagonally across the field in 2 frames, holds, then thins
layers.notes: the main shape is black; it crosses the sky line so it reads at any distance

layers.motion: dark grey-violet moon sphere inside the wedge with a dark figure silhouette, rim lit
layers.notes: a quiet symbolic shape inside the slash

layers.motion: 4-5 parallel thin streaks along the wedge edges, scroll forward fast
layers.notes: bright edges on a dark body

layers.motion: butterfly/petal confetti scattered along the wedge, drag 2, slow fall
low dust cloud along the ground, drag 3, life 1.2 s
medium shake on wedge arrival

whyItLooksGood: A small precise cue (ring at the hand, then a flat line) contrasts with the screen-crossing black wedge that follows
The wedge is a single black graphic shape crossing the horizon; it reads even from a far gameplay camera
Bright thin streaks only on the wedge edges: dark body, hot outline
The moon-and-figure inside the slash adds a story element without extra motion
buildNotes: Video 0:15.9-0:17.7 (gameplay camera, no cuts). Hand sigil: createRing 0.6 m with a small GlowSphere core, then tween scale-y to 0.05 while scale-x grows to 5 (becomes the flare line). Release: a custom long wedge mesh (normal blend, unlit black, alpha-erosion along its length for the exit) placed diagonally from above the caster down toward the target; a crescent trail-ribbon swirl around the caster. Inside the wedge: a GlowSphere-sized dark sphere with a rim-light shader and a silhouette sprite. 4-5 additive thin ribbons along the wedge edges with fast scrolling UV. Emitter of butterfly sprites. Dust: normal-blended grey-violet smoke, drag 3. Exaggerate the wedge length so it spans the arena.

name: Dash crescent and spike: dash to target, magenta crescent slash, second crescent with a white ground spike, rising dotted pillar with a black diamond tip

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:18.8-0:21.0. The caster crouches and dashes across the field to the target with no VFX trail at all

phases.name: release
phases.what: on arrival a vertical magenta crescent slash flashes over the target with a pink glow pool on the ground (0.9), fades over 0.3 s with a few sparks rising

phases.name: impact
phases.what: a second, bigger crescent arcs over the target and a sharp white spike stabs up from the ground beside it

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: a thin vertical line of pink dots rises 6-8 m above the target with a small black diamond at its tip, then fades; the pink ground pool fades last

layers.motion: vertical crescent 2.5 m, drawn in 2 frames, erodes over 0.3 s
layers.notes: thick at the middle, thin tips

layers.motion: pink glow pool 2 m under the target, fades over 1.2 s

buildNotes: Video 0:18.8-0:21.0 (gameplay camera). Move the caster to the target over 0.6 s. Crescents: half-ring meshes with an alpha-erosion shader, additive, oriented vertically and facing the camera, the second one 40% bigger and rotated 30 degrees. Ground pool: additive ground-decal. Spike: a thin cone mesh scaling y 0 -> 1 in 1 frame. Dotted pillar: 12 small additive dot sprites spaced 0.5 m that appear bottom to top over 0.4 s, plus a small black octahedron at the top (normal blend). Light shake on the second crescent.

name: Sky rift blade rain: pink shard cluster tears open above, then six long black-violet blades rake diagonally down across the field

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:23.4-0:25.8. A flat horizontal pink flare at the caster's hand (0.1 s), the caster raises one arm, small pink motes rise from it

phases.name: release
phases.what: above and behind the caster a jagged cluster of pink-white crystal shards and lightning-like cracks tears open in the sky and grows for 0.3 s

phases.name: impact
phases.what: six long parallel black-violet blades with bright pink-white edges rake diagonally down from the rift across the field, a magenta swirl whips around the caster

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: the blades hang in place as long dark streaks and slowly fade, a low violet dust cloud rolls on the ground, purple petal motes drift

layers.motion: flat horizontal flare line at hand, 2 frames
jagged crack lines plus a cluster of small crystal shards spreading outward in the sky over 0.3 s, flicker every 2 frames
layers.notes: the rift is drawn as cracks in the air, which sets up where the blades come from

layers.motion: 6 long thin blade wedges (15-20 m), parallel, offset 0.8 m, arrive 1 frame apart from the rift down to the ground
layers.notes: dark bodies with hot pink-white edges; parallel lines read like a claw rake

layers.motion: thick magenta swirl around the caster, 1 turn in 0.2 s
ground dust rolling out from the blade landing line, drag 3, life 1.2 s
petal motes drifting down slowly, life 1.5 s
medium shake when the blades land

whyItLooksGood: The source of the attack (the sky rift) appears 0.3 s before the blades, so the viewer looks up and then follows the blades down
Six parallel dark blades arriving one frame apart read as a single rake but with texture
The blades hang and fade slowly (1.2 s) instead of vanishing, so the aftermath reads as scars in the air
buildNotes: Video 0:23.4-0:25.8 (gameplay camera). Rift: a cluster of 15 small additive pink shard quads plus 3-4 jagged lightning-arc polylines at a point 6 m above and behind the caster, growing outward over 0.3 s. Blades: 6 custom thin wedge meshes (normal blend, near-black violet) each with an additive edge ribbon, spawned 1 frame apart along parallel diagonals from the rift to a line through the target point; hold, then alpha-erode over 1.2 s. Swirl: trail-ribbon around the caster. Dust: normal Emitter along the landing line. Medium camera shake on landing.

name: Rune fireball summon: spark-drawn pentagram, white glint flare, starburst ignition and a sustained bonfire orb that collapses into smoke

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:00.0-0:06.0 (repeats at 0:06.0, 0:12.6 and 0:19.3). A small bright spark runs around the ground and draws a thin pink-red circle with a pentagram inside (0-0.25), then a white four-point glint with a long horizontal flare line flashes 1.5 m above the circle centre (0.25-0.42)

phases.name: release
phases.what: a huge orange-white starburst flash with long spike rays explodes over the circle (fills ~40% of the frame for 2 frames)

phases.name: impact
phases.what: a fireball forms 1 m above the circle; 2 white hollow ring pops and a star glint at its centre; the rune circle turns to a thick glowing orange ring on the ground

phases.name: sustain
phases.what: a 2 m flickering fire orb (white-yellow core, orange-red flame tongues) burns over a dark scorched ring, constant ember spray and thin dark smoke wisps

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: the orb breaks up inside a swirling dark smoke shell (0.4 s), then only grey smoke wisps, a dark arc swirl and a few embers remain; clean at ~6.0

layers.motion: thin circle and pentagram drawn progressively by a moving spark over 0.25 s (reveal by angle)
layers.notes: drawing the circle on screen is the telegraph; it is faster and more readable than a fade-in

layers.motion: four-point star glint with a long horizontal flare streak (4 m), 2-3 frames, above the circle centre
layers.notes: a cold white glint before the warm fire: temperature contrast on the cue

layers.motion: spiky starburst sprite 4-5 m, 2 frames, random ray lengths
2 thin white hollow rings pop around the forming fireball, 0.5 -> 1.5 m in 0.15 s
fire orb 2 m, flipbook flame sprites stacked, flicker scale 0.9-1.1
layers.notes: flame tongues with ragged dark-red edges

layers.motion: embers sprayed outward and up, gravity -1, drag 1, life 0.8 s, stretched
thin dark wisps rising from the top of the flame, slow
dark scorched ring with glowing orange cracks at the rune edge
smoke shell swirls around the dying fire (spin), then rises and thins, life 1.2 s
layers.notes: the collapse is shown, not cut

whyItLooksGood: The telegraph is drawn by a moving spark, so the viewer's eye follows a point around the circle and is already looking at the spot when it ignites
A cold white glint with a long horizontal flare right before the warm starburst gives a crisp 'tick' that the fire then answers
The sustained orb has a dark smoke and dark scorch frame, so it stays readable on a grey floor for 4 s
The exit is a smoke collapse with a swirl, so the effect ends with motion rather than a fade
buildNotes: Video 0:00.0-0:06.0. Rune: a ground-plane circle plus pentagram texture with a shader uniform revealing it by polar angle (0 -> 360 in 0.25 s), plus a tiny GlowSphere spark moving along the circle edge. Glint: an additive four-point star sprite with a long horizontal streak quad, 3 frames. Ignition: big starburst sprite 2 frames plus FinishPass impact flash at low strength; 2 createRing hollow rings popping. Orb: GlowSphere core plus 6-8 flame flipbook billboards around it with random rotation and flicker; ember Emitter (gravity -1, drag 1); normal-blended smoke wisps; scorch decal with emissive orange cracks. Collapse at 4.6 s: shrink the flames, spawn a spinning smoke-shell Emitter (spin 3, drag 2) and a dark arc ribbon, then let embers die out. For targeting: place the circle at the clicked ground point; the orb can then damage enemies in a 3 m radius per tick.

name: Dark lord slash: red-tinted wind-up burst, a crouch hold, then a full-screen red hit with glitch cubes and damage digits that leaves a grey dust vortex

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: video 0:06.1-0:08.0 (same move at 0:00.65, 0:03.65 and 0:08.4). The world tints pink-red in 1 frame; a red crescent wind-up slash with black spikes flashes around the character, then a red sphere with a black core bursts and a white wind ring spins around it; the tint fades

phases.name: release
phases.what: the character holds a crouched pose with no effect at all for ~0.13 s (a deliberate dead beat)

phases.name: impact
phases.what: full-screen red tint again, an orange-white starburst at the target, black cubes and long red speed streaks blast outward, red glitch digits flash, a red smear disc spins on the ground

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: the disc becomes a ragged red-black ring with a grey wind spiral, orange sparks skid along the ground away from it; then only a grey normal-blended dust vortex spins and fades over ~0.8 s

layers.motion: full-screen pink-red multiply tint, on in 1 frame, fades over 0.3 s; again on the impact
layers.notes: the world goes red twice, once per beat

layers.motion: red crescent slash with black spike fringe around the character, 2 frames
red sphere with black core 1.5 m, pops 0 -> 1 in 2 frames, a white wind ring spins around it
big spiky starburst at the target, 2 frames
15-25 small black cubes flung outward and slightly up, spin, drag 2, life 0.4 s
layers.notes: flat black cubes read as glitch/void fragments, not rocks

layers.motion: long horizontal red speed streaks shooting out sideways, life 0.15 s
red digit sprites (random numbers) flashing in the smear for 3-4 frames
layers.notes: damage-number glyphs used as texture, a glitch/digital flavour

layers.motion: spinning red smear disc 6 m, then a ragged red ring with a black inner edge
3-5 orange sparks skidding along the ground away from the ring, drag 1
grey dust vortex disc spinning on the ground, 5 m, fades over 0.8 s
layers.notes: grey, not red: the colour leaves first, the motion stays

layers.motion: heavy shake on the impact, a camera lurch toward the hit on the wind-up

whyItLooksGood: Two beats with a dead hold between them: the 0.13 s crouch with no VFX makes the second hit land much harder than the first
The whole world tinting red on both beats does the work of a flash without white, and the red-black-white palette stays strict
Glitch cubes and red digits give the slash a 'corrupted' identity that ordinary sparks would not
The colour drains before the motion: the grey dust vortex keeps spinning after the red is gone, which is a clean, calm exit
buildNotes: Video 0:06.1-0:08.0. Wind-up: FinishPass colour tint (#ff3a4a multiply) for 0.3 s; crescent ribbon with black spike fringe (normal blend) around the caster; GlowSphere with a black core and red rim, plus a white wind ring (createRing with a streaky texture, spinning). Hold: 0.13 s with nothing (keep the caster in a crouch pose). Impact: second tint; starburst sprite; instanced black cube debris (normal blend, spin, drag 2); stretched red streak Emitter shooting sideways; a few sprites with digit textures (canvas-generated numbers) flashing for 3-4 frames; spinning red ground decal that becomes a ragged ring (alpha-erosion). Aftermath: ground spark skid Emitter; normal-blended grey dust ring that spins (rotate the decal or a smoke Emitter with tangential velocity) and fades over 0.8 s. Heavy shake on the impact frame. Exaggerate the hold; it must feel like a pause.
